standard.title: Share artworks in informal settings
standard.description: share artworks and/or visual arts practice in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share artworks with an audience and say something about the work (AC9AVAFP01). They have basic experience of informal sharing with peers and the teacher. They have not yet made deliberate decisions about audience, context or presentation format.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share artworks and/or visual arts practice in informal settings, making choices about audience and ways to share.

nodes.label: Deciding how and with whom to share
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify different ways and audiences for sharing artworks — from sharing with a friend to sharing with the whole class or online with families.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different ways or audiences for sharing an artwork and choose one.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of sharing options (class, small group, school LMS, teacher, family); choose an appropriate audience and format for a specific artwork; explain the choice.
wider: Post an artwork or work-in-progress on the school learning management system with a short explanation — consider what families can understand about the work from the image and text
Decide whether to share a finished work or a work-in-progress, and explain what sharing at each stage communicates to the audience

response_modes.reason: Students at this level default to 'show everyone' without considering what different sharing contexts involve. Structured prompts ('Who would understand this work best? What do you want people to know about it?') build deliberate decision-making.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two different ways or audiences for sharing an artwork
Makes a choice and gives a reason for it

nodes.label: Sharing and explaining
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share an artwork or visual arts practice in an informal setting and explain what they like, what they made or what the work communicates.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one artwork in an informal setting and explain one thing — what they like, what it shows, or how they made it.
nodes.typical_width: Share artworks and visual arts practice in multiple informal settings; explain choices, ideas and processes; respond to questions; participate in peer activities that involve explaining and interpreting works.
wider: Dramatise the making of a work — use gesture and movement to communicate the creative process for an audience, then select the most successful section and frame it for display
Participate in a peer activity where everyday-object artworks are matched to their objects — explain how you interpreted the visual personification choices made

response_modes.reason: Different sharing formats demand different explanatory moves. The dramatised presentation, the gallery-walk, and the work-in-progress review each require students to communicate in distinct ways — a range of formats builds versatile presentational capability.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The dramatised presentation format is particularly rich — students perform the creative process itself as an artwork, developing metacognitive awareness of their own making that feeds back into future creating.
success_criteria: Shares at least one artwork in an informal setting
Explains at least one thing — what they like, what the work shows, or how they made it
